step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify Nodes: Visual elements drawn include Coach (web/desktop user icon), Member (mobile user icon), Chime SDK, Cognito, API Gateway, Lambda, Aurora, DynamoDB, Kinesis, and S3.
2. Identify Actor Nodes: 'Member' is an external mobile end-user (UserConsumerMobile). 'Coach' represents internal/operational studio staff (UserCompanyDeveloper).
3. Exact Services: Map Chime SDK to 'Chime', Kinesis to 'KinesisDataStream', API Gateway to 'ApiGateway', Lambda to 'Lambda', Aurora to 'Aurora', DynamoDB to 'DynamoDB', S3 to 'S3', Cognito to 'Cognito'.
4. Map Edges based on arrows:
   - Coach and Member authenticate via Cognito.
   - Member interacts with API Gateway, triggering Lambda to read/write class info from Aurora and workout summaries from DynamoDB.
   - Real-time video/audio and WebSocket heart rate streaming flow bidirectionally between Member, Chime SDK, and Coach.
   - Heart rate and summary data streams from Member to Kinesis, which dumps into S3.

edges.notes: Member requests class details via API Gateway
Lambda fetches class info from Aurora
Lambda returns response to API Gateway
API Gateway returns class info to Member
Member sends video/audio and heart rate data to Chime SDK
Chime SDK streams member video and heart rate tiles to Coach
Coach streams video and audio instructions to Chime SDK
Chime SDK streams coach feed and exercise video to Member
Member streams second-by-second telemetry and workout summary to Kinesis
Kinesis persists data into S3 Data Lake
Lambda stores summary info in DynamoDB
DynamoDB provides summary info back for member mobile review
